raised_by: CC, while measuring the corpus-wide reorg residue at the close of the-loop-names-its-own-staleness-instead-of-benching-a-device
question: build_inspector's promotion sieves (charted_refs_resolve, survey_holdings_resolve, constraint_traces) read EVERY packet a component ever berthed. Is the invariant 'every chart this component ever made still resolves' (A), or 'the chart of the voyage being promoted still resolves' (B)?
whats_beyond: 306 of the 307 standing findings are one cause: the rung move and the chart dissolution moved files under packets that were TRUE when berthed. Under A they are all real findings and a bulk move must forward everything or the corpus stays red permanently. Under B most are not findings at all — they are old charts of finished voyages the gate should not be re-judging — and the cost of B is that the historical record stops being checked, so a year-old chart pointing at nothing becomes ordinary rather than red. The practical stake is that a promotion gate reporting 306 residue findings is a gate readers learn to skim, and its founding failure (2026-07-24: 'done' reported while the files stood unmoved) is exactly what a skimmed gate stops catching.
why_it_is_not_answerable_from_the_corpus: The charter narrows it and does not close it. 'Promotion judges a build AGAINST its chart' — singular, possessive — is reading B about the SEAT. But the same charter calls `inspect()` with no component 'the whole-repo sweep', which has no current build, and these sieves are in SIEVES so they run there; the code loops over every orient packet the component ever berthed, which is reading A. The charter's words say B about the seat, the code says A about the corpus, and the two never contradict because the distinction was not drawn when either was written. Reading the implementation back as intent is the one direction the record says not to reason in.
source: cairn/machines/build_inspector/intention+why.json; cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py::charted_refs_resolve; ticket a-bulk-move-forwards-itself-from-gits-own-rename-record (which carries the full measurement and is BLOCKED on this for its disposition half only — its derivation half is buildable under either reading)

resolved.answer: B — a sieve measures what is needed to prove THE THING, not every component ever berthed. Each workflow could be unique, so checking every historical chart is not needed. 306 of 307 standing findings are old voyages the sieve should not be re-measuring. The sieve measures the promoting voyage's chart.
resolved.source: Akien, 2026-08-19: "a single sieve measures whatever is needed to prove the thing. do we need to check every component ever berthed given that each workflow could be unique? probably not."
